note: streaming TTFT (time to first SSE event, HTTP-observed) vs non-streaming time-to-full-response (HTTP-observed p50 elapsed), same concurrency, same prompt/settings as prior loadtests
honest_finding: Streaming's TTFT advantage over non-streaming is real but shrinks sharply as concurrency grows (41% faster at c=10 down to 9.5% at c=50) -- because max_batch_size=4 means most of TTFT at higher concurrency is admission queueing delay, not generation time, and streaming can't make a request start being processed any sooner, only reveal its first token sooner once it IS being processed. Throughput is roughly a wash at c=10 and slightly lower for streaming at c=20/50 (37.3-37.5 vs 41.0-41.5 tok/s) -- plausible mechanism: per-token SSE framing/flush overhead (json.dumps + HTTP chunk write per token) adds real per-token cost that a single buffered response at the end doesn't pay, though the gap is within a few tok/s and noisier than v0.3/v0.4's negative results.
